SUMMARY & RECOMMENDATIONS

In normal times, the Shanghai market consumes some
three million tons annually of bituminous coal, supplies being
drawn primarily from mines situated along the Tientsin-Pukow
Railway, the Shantung coal field and the Kailan Mines.

It is estimated that in terms of present-day conditions
the market consumption of bituminous coal will be approximately
two million tons annually. No supplies can be relied upon from
Tientsin-Pukow Railway or Shantung mines for some little time
to come. Your Committee has been informed that it is virtually
impossible for Kailan Mines to supply more than 900,000 to
1,000,000 tons annually, of which figures 900,000 is more likely
to represent actual achievement.

There appears, therefore, a quantity of up to one
million tons which has to be found elsewhere, and after deducting
imports which it is understood will be made independently by
utility companies and larger concerns, there will be a not in-
considerable quantity required to be imported for distribution
to that section of the public which has no facilities for pro-
tecting its own interests. In the past the largest dealer
catering to this type of business has been Noo Tai Shing.

It is thought that the tonnage of imports from abroad
necessary to protect requirements (irrespective of Utility Com-
panies) for the coming Winter (November 1938 to February 1939)
will be between 100,000 to 200,000 tons.

It is suggested that financial assistance by the Council
to this end will not be necessary, but co-operation and help by
the Fuel Committee, in return for some measure of supervisory
control, is deemed necessary under the following headings:-
page_data.zh:
-7-

摘要与建议

在正常时期，上海市场每年消耗约三百万吨烟煤，供应主要来自津浦铁路沿线、山东煤田和开滦煤矿。

据估计，按当前状况，市场烟煤消费量约为每年两百万吨。在未来一段时间内，无法指望从津浦铁路或山东煤矿获得任何供应。本委员会获悉，开滦煤矿每年实际上不可能供应超过 900,000 至 1,000,000 吨，其中 900,000 吨更可能代表实际达成量。

因此，似乎有多达一百万吨的数量需要从其他地方寻找，在扣除据悉将由公用事业公司和大型商号独立进行的进口后，仍有相当数量的煤炭需要进口，以分配给那些没有能力保护自身利益的公众部分。过去，从事此类业务最大的经销商是 Neo Tai Shing（音译：新泰兴）。

据认为，为保障即将到来的冬季（1938 年 11 月至 1939 年 2 月）的需求（不包括公用事业公司），所需的海外进口吨位将在 100,000 至 200,000 吨之间。

建议工部局无需为此提供财政援助，但燃料委员会的合作与帮助被视为必要，作为交换，需实施一定程度的监管控制，具体如下：

page_data.en:
-8-
(1) Ascertaining the reliability of sources of supply
abroad with particular regard to the suitability of
coal to be purchased.
(2) Assistance where necessary for arranging shipping and
discharging facilities.
(3) Giving advice and any assistance required in arranging
suitable terms of payment.

Your Committee delegated Mr. Watts to enquire of
Messrs. Nee Tai Shing whether or not that firm proposed to make
imports of foreign coal and to seek his opinion as to the
necessity therefor.

The opinion of Nee Tai Shing regarding the quantity
required for the coming Winter closely approximates the figure
of 200,000 tons given above. Nee Tai Shing's representative
pointed out, however, that in view of:-
(1) the high prices at which this coal will be landed,
(2) possible competition from casual buyers and such
organisations as the Kailan Mining Administration and
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, and the further possibility,
admittedly rather remote at the present time, of Shan-
tung coals finding their way to Shanghai,
(3) the general uncertainty of the situation,
he is prepared to consider this business, but based on a safe
total figure which is unlikely to involve him in a loss.

Mr. Watts explained to Nee Tai Shing that there could
be no question of the Council sponsoring the import of coal by
any one firm or group of individuals, but that he thought it
likely that, if the Fuel Committee could inform the Council that
they were satisfied winter supplies were reasonably adequately
protected it was probable that no organised competition would be
forthcoming from that body.

Mr. Watts further pointed out that the Kailan Mining
Administration was not in principle desirous of handling coal
other than its own and would not interfere with any business
undertaken by Nee Tai Shing, provided always he did not work to
an unreasonable profit which might make it difficult for the
Kailan Mining Administration to refuse a request from the Council
page_data.zh:
-8-
(1) 核实海外供应来源的可靠性，特别关注拟购煤炭的适用性。
(2) 在必要时协助安排航运和卸货设施。
(3) 就安排合适的付款条款提供建议及所需任何协助。

本委员会委派 Watts 先生向 Nee Tai Shing（音译：新泰兴）商行查询，该商行是否计划进口外国煤炭，并征求其对此必要性的意见。

Nee Tai Shing 关于今冬所需数量的意见与上述 200,000 吨的数字非常接近。然而，Nee Tai Shing 的代表指出，鉴于：
(1) 该煤炭到岸价格高昂，
(2) 可能面临零星买家以及开滦矿务局和三井物产株式会社等组织的竞争，以及山东煤炭流入上海的可能性（尽管目前看来这种可能性较遥远），
(3) 局势普遍存在不确定性，
他准备考虑此项业务，但基于一个稳妥的总量数字，该数字不太可能使他遭受损失。

Watts 先生向 Nee Tai Shing 解释，工部局绝无可能赞助任何一家商行或个人团体进口煤炭，但他认为，如果燃料委员会能够告知工部局，他们对冬季供应得到合理充分的保障感到满意，那么该机构很可能不会发起有组织的竞争。

Watts 先生进一步指出，开滦矿务局原则上不希望处理非自产煤炭，只要 Nee Tai Shing 不追求不合理的利润，致使开滦矿务局难以拒绝工部局要求其自行进口以稳定价格的请求，开滦矿务局就不会干涉 Nee Tai Shing 开展的任何业务。

to import themselves with a view to stabilising prices.
The question of competition by the M.B.K. and Shantung
coals was then discussed with Nge Tai Shing's representative and
for a variety of reasons deemed to be unlikely under current con-
ditions.
Nge Tai Shing is satisfied in view of the foregoing that
the import of foreign coals by him is a reasonable business risk
and venture, and has already placed orders abroad for 15,000/25,000
tons which will arrive in Shanghai between August and October. It
is hoped that this figure will be increased to 30,000 tons and
that this total quantity will be in stock before the winter.
Thereafter he is in principle prepared to bring in a further
70,000 tons, provided he feels assured of a profit, which will
make a grand total of 100,000 tons to help to protect the anti-
cipated winter shortage.
Nge Tai Shing is prepared to co-operate with the Fuel
Committee's representative in return for no competition on the
part of the Kailan Mining Administration, and is further prepared
to work to a profit of up to ten percent on the business undertaken.
Your Committee is therefore of the opinion that the
organised imports contemplated by Nge Tai Shing and the casual
purchases by other merchants and dealers (exclusive of the Power
Company who, we understand, are endeavouring to make arrangements
to cover their own requirements by importations from abroad)
are likely to prevent a serious shortage during the winter months.
There is unlikely however, to be an abundance of coal on account of
the high price of imported stocks, unless the Council is prepared
to hold a reserve for the benefit of the community. This, your
Committee does not recommend or deem necessary at the present
time.

随后与 Nge Tai Shing（音译：新泰兴）的代表讨论了三井物产株式会社（M.B.K.）和山东煤炭的竞争问题，出于多种原因，认为在当前条件下这种情况不太可能发生。

鉴于上述情况，Nge Tai Shing 确信由其进口外国煤炭是一项合理的商业风险和举措，并已在国外下达了 15,000/25,000 吨的订单，这些煤炭将于八月至十月间抵达上海。希望这一数字能增加到 30,000 吨，并且这批总量能在冬季前入库。此后，原则上他准备再引进 70,000 吨，前提是他对利润感到放心，这将使总数达到 100,000 吨，以帮助缓解预期的冬季短缺。

Nge Tai Shing 准备与燃料委员会代表合作，以换取开滦矿务局不进行竞争，并进一步准备在所开展的业务中获取高达百分之十的利润。

因此，本委员会认为，Nge Tai Shing 计划的有组织进口以及其他商人和经销商的零星采购（不包括电力公司，据我们所知，该公司正努力通过从国外进口来满足自身需求），可能会防止冬季月份出现严重短缺。

然而，由于进口库存价格高昂，煤炭不太可能出现充裕供应，除非工部局愿意为社区利益持有储备。本委员会目前不建议也不认为有必要这样做。

requirements in this category.

In our opinion, the danger of insufficient supplies
of coal is not so great as the danger of high prices should
the majority of supplies consist of foreign coal, the fob value
and freight of which have to be paid in £ Sterling.

On the other hand, it is to be expected that competi-
tion between the various foreign coals imported to complete the
needs of our market, will prevent importers from selling at
prices too much in excess of their cost price, but the latter
will be governed by the rate of exchange of the local currency,
by the rate of freight and by the amount of customs duty to be
paid in dollars.

We are, dear Sir,

Yours faithfully,

SOCIETE FRANCAISE DES CHARBONNAGES DU TONKIN
page_data.zh:
2.

如果开滦矿务局无法满足本地对软煤的全部需求——这是意料之中的事——那么此类煤炭关税的大幅降低必将促进从加尔各答、婆罗洲、德兰士瓦和澳大利亚的进口（我们认为日本没有任何可供出口的煤炭）。

就无烟煤而言，源自 Hongay 及印度支那小型矿井的煤炭应能满足该类别的所有需求。

在我们看来，煤炭供应不足的危险并不像价格高昂的危险那么大，假如大部分供应由外国煤炭组成，其离岸价值（fob value）和运费必须以英镑支付。

另一方面，可以预期，为满足我方市场需求而进口的各种外国煤炭之间的竞争，将防止进口商以远高于成本价的价格出售，但后者将受当地货币汇率、运费率以及需以美元支付的关税数额所制约。

尊敬的先生，此致，

敬礼，

东京湾法国煤矿公司

PRICE OF COAL BRIQUETTES AGAIN INCREASED

The stocks of hard and soft coal in Shanghai

coal in the various godowns in Hongkew, the Western District

1940

Indo-China Supply Due
Coal Prices
Decline On
Local Market

For the first time in several weeks, coal prices declined on the local market yesterday as large holdings were dumped into the market and huge quantities of the fuel were expected in the city from Indo-China.

Trading quarters stated yesterday that more than 300,000 tons of coal are at present storaged in local coal yards, this amount being sufficient for one and a half months' use.

Dealers who had large holdings were seen during the past two weeks releasing their ware into the market in view of the declining prices.

According to dealers, the declines in prices were partly due to the unusually warm weather in the city, thus causing a smaller demand for coal, and partly due to unexpected coal import activities, imports since the beginning of October having totaled more than 120,000 tons.

Responsible quarters were optimistic that the city this winter would face no coal shortage, and most probably would see no substantial increase in the price of coal even if cold weather set in.

Although condition in French Indo-China is becoming increasingly critical, the same quarters were of the opinion that barring open hostilities between Siam and the French colony, coal shipment to Shanghai would not be seriously affected.

Coal briquette prices, an essential commodity for the city's less well-to-do residents, also have declined slightly. Coal hongs are quoting briquettes at from $140 to $150 per ton, representing a $10 to $20 decline since the early part of November.

Bituminous coal is selling in local hongs at about $200 per ton and anthracite coal at about $260 per ton.

（批：Coal files）

因印度支那供应将至
本地市场
煤价下跌

由于大量持仓被抛售入市，且预计将有大量燃料从印度支那运抵本市，本地市场煤价昨日数周来首次下跌。

交易界人士昨日表示，目前本地煤场储存的煤炭超过300,000吨，这一数量足够使用一个半月。

在过去两周里，拥有大量持仓的经销商因价格下跌而被看到向市场释放其仓储货物。

据经销商称，价格下跌部分原因是本市异常温暖的天气，导致煤炭需求减少，部分原因是出乎意料的煤炭进口活动，自十月初以来的进口总量已超过120,000吨。

有关方面乐观地认为，本市今冬不会面临煤炭短缺，即使天气变冷，煤价也很可能不会出现大幅上涨。

尽管法属印度支那的局势日益危急，但同一方面的意见认为，除非暹罗（Siam）与法国殖民地之间爆发公开敌对行动，否则运往上海的煤炭 shipment 不会受到严重影响。

作为本市较贫困居民必需品的煤球价格也略有下降。煤行报价为每吨140至150美元，代表自11月初以来下降了10至20美元。

烟煤在本地煤行的售价约为每吨200美元，无烟煤约为每吨260美元。

20 11 44

29-10-40 P.M.
Manichi

COAL SUPPLIES FROM THE HWAINAN MINES.

More than 1,000,000,000 tons of coal are being kept in the Hwainan Mining Region, which includes the Kowloon (九龍), Tatung (大通), and Tungshan Coal Mines, and in the Zang Yao (上窯) and Sincheng (新成) Mining Regions. This mining region is the largest in Central China. The Hwainan Coal Mining Company, which is controlled by the Japanese Government, has been steadily proceeding with its five year plan, with the result that 1,500 to 1,600 tons of coal are now being mined everyday.

The transportation of the coal has been by the Hwai River only, but when the river is at flood, not more than 300 to 400 tons of coal can be transported. In winter, the river is so shallow that much less coal can be transported, in which event Shanghai and Nanking will suffer a coal famine.

In view of these circumstances, the Hwainan Coal Mining Company has requested the Central China Railway Company to hasten the repairs to a section of the Hwainan Railway from Dien Kia Yen (田家庵) via Luchow (廬州) to Yu Chi Kou (裕溪口). When this work has been completed about 1,500 to 1,600 tons of coal can be transported daily by the Hwainan Railway as from November 1.

On the completion of the five year plan it is expected that as much as 2,000,000 tons of coal can be transported annually and the scarcity of coal in Shanghai, Nanking etc. will be considerably alleviated.

A coal-yard has been constructed at Yu Chi Kou and will be opened at 10 a.m. (Japanese time) on November 3.

《每日新闻》（Manichi）

来自淮南煤矿的煤炭供应。

淮南矿区，包括九龙（九龍）、大通（Tatung）和东山（Tungshan）煤矿，以及上窑（Zang Yao）和新成（Sincheng）矿区，储藏着超过10亿吨煤炭。该矿区是华中最大的矿区。由日本政府控制的淮南煤矿公司一直在稳步推进其五年计划，结果是现在每天开采1,500至1,600吨煤炭。

煤炭运输仅通过淮河进行，但当河水泛滥时，运输的煤炭不超过300至400吨。冬季，河水很浅，运输的煤炭更少，在这种情况下，上海和南京将遭受煤荒。

鉴于这些情况，淮南煤矿公司已请求华中铁路公司加快修复从田家庵（Dien Kia Yen）经庐州（Luchow）到裕溪口（Yu Chi Kou）的一段淮南铁路。当这项工作完成后，从11月1日起，淮南铁路每天可运输约1,500至1,600吨煤炭。

预计五年计划完成后，每年可运输多达2,000,000吨煤炭，上海、南京等地的煤炭短缺状况将大大缓解。

裕溪口已建有一个煤场，将于11月3日上午10时（日本时间）开放。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

MAY 2, 1940

Bath Houses Hit by
High Coal Costs
Petition Made to Chamber
Of Commerce

The increased price of coal is now affecting public health because public bath houses numbering about 100 in Shanghai are in urgent need of cheap coal without which they may close business. This information is contained in a petition sent by the Shanghai Bath House Trade Association to the Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai, urging the latter to secure more coal for members of the Association as it has been doing for boiled water supplying shops.

It is revealed in this petition that the Association has sent requests to civic leaders and coal mining companies for the supply of cheap coal but so far no result has been obtained. It is pointed out that public bath houses where most Chinese without modern equipment at home go for bathing, need 10 times as much coal as boiled water supplying shops where the Chinese obtain their drinking water.

If no cheap coal is forthcoming, bath house managers cannot continue their business and many persons will be rendered jobless, it is stated. It is argued that while the Shanghai Coal Merchants' Association has decided to give 800 tons of coal to hot water shops monthly, bath houses should also receive its attention as they also affect the public. The Chamber is urged to negotiate with coal merchants so that more coal may be obtained by bath houses.

CHINESE CHAMBER OF COMMERCE REQUESTS S.M.C. TO NEGOTIATE
WITH STEAMSHIP COMPANIES FOR REDUCTION IN FREIGHT OF COAL
DUST

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce has sent
the following letter to the Shanghai Municipal Council:-
"As coal briquettes are the main fuel
used by the Shanghai people, their shortage affects the
public very much. This Chamber has negotiated with the
Machine-Made Coal Briquette Traders' Guild, asking the
latter to double its efforts in the production of coal
briquettes and to reduce the price of same. It must be
understood that coal dust, the raw material required for
the making of coal briquettes, comes entirely from French
Indo-China. About 1,000 tons per day, i.e. 30,000 tons a
month, are transported to Shanghai from Haiphong. Recently
the freights charged by the steam navigation companies
increased sharply and this affected the cost of production
of coal briquettes. This is, indeed, an obstacle to efforts
to reduce the price of coal briquettes. The Chinese
Chamber of Commerce and the Machine-Made Coal Briquette
Traders' Guild agree that the sole solution is to ask the
S.M.C. to hold a meeting with the steam navigation companies
to negotiate a reduction in freight for the transportation
of coal dust, so that coal briquette factories may have a
chance to double their efforts to produce and sell at a
cheaper price. As this is a matter of public welfare, we
are sure that the Council will agree to this suggestion."

CHINA PRESS.
MAR 6 1940

$200 A Ton For Freight
Prices Of Coal In Shanghai
Not Expected To Decline

Despite the scheduled arrival of huge quantities of coal from India and French Indo-China, local fuel traders predicted yesterday that the prices of imported coal, now soaring beyond $250 per ton, were not expected to decline.
Traders pointed out that in view of the fact that freight charges alone cost importers of Indian coal $200 per ton, retail prices of the fuel would remain essentially the same with the arrival of the new shipments.
It was asserted that arrivals of imported coal continued to be in large quantities during the past two months although the price kept on climbing.
Customs reports for January, it was stated, revealed that 208,852 tons of coal arrived in Shanghai. The imports were valued at $3,446,896, the majority of them having been shipped here from Japanese ports.

More Coal Due Here
Local trading reports stated yesterday that about 100,000 tons of anthracite and bituminous coal had been ordered by local dealers from India and French Indo-China and that they were expected to arrive here before the middle of the month.
Meanwhile, the general situation in the local fuel market was reported to have shown a noticeable improvement following brisk unloading by holders of stocks. In view of these developments it was expected that the tension recently experienced would ease considerably in the near future.
Reports were received yesterday that the previous petition of the City Chamber of Commerce for approval for the shipment of 30,000 piculs of charcoal from the east Chekiang area to Shanghai had been granted by the Chekiang Provincial Government.

Sales Continued
Cheap sales of coal briquettes continued yesterday with 26 shops participating. The amount sold yesterday, as on previous days, was 1,000 piculs and buyers were restricted to purchase 20 cents' worth each.
The briquettes thus sold is supplied by 14 members of the local Machine Made Coal Briquette Manufacturers' Guild who have jointly consented to appropriate 20,000 piculs for the purpose.
Officials in charge of the sales stated yesterday that if the sales proved successful when the entire amount had been exhausted, more supplies were said to be available.

运费每吨200美元
上海煤价预计不会下跌

尽管预定将有大量煤炭从印度和法属印度支那运抵，当地燃料商昨日预测，目前飙升超过每吨250美元的进口煤价预计不会下跌。
商人指出，鉴于仅运费一项就使印度煤进口商每吨承担200美元的成本，随着新货到达，该燃料的零售价格将基本保持不变。
据称，尽管价格持续攀升，过去两个月进口煤的到货量依然巨大。
据悉，1月份的海关报告显示，有208,852吨煤炭运抵上海。进口总值为3,446,896美元，其中大部分是从日本港口装运至此。

更多煤炭即将运抵此地
当地贸易报告昨日称，当地商行已从印度和法属印度支那订购了约10万吨无烟煤和烟煤，预计将于本月中旬前运抵此地。
与此同时，据报道，随着存货持有者加紧卸货，当地燃料市场的总体状况已有明显改善。鉴于这些发展，预计近期经历的紧张局势将在不久的将来大大缓解。
昨日收到报告称，市商会此前关于批准从浙东地区向上海装运30,000担木炭的申请已获浙江省政府批准。

销售持续
昨日煤球平价销售继续进行，共有26家店铺参与。昨日的销售量与前几日相同，为1,000担，每位买家限购价值20角的煤球。
如此销售的煤球由本地机制煤球制造业同业公会的14家会员提供，他们已共同同意拨出20,000担用于此目的。
负责销售的官员昨日表示，如果当全部存量售完后销售情况证明成功，据说将有更多供应可用。

FEB 1 4 1940
Coal Situation in Shanghai
Has Gloomy Outlook
High Shipping Rates Responsible for Abnormal
Soaring Cost ; Little Profit to Dealers
SPECIAL TO THE "N.C.D.N."
SHANGHAI is in a bad way at present as far as coal is concerned, with that precious commodity selling on the market at the unbelievable price of $220 a ton. And the future holds no relief in sight, as the price of coal is climbing steadily from week to week. Now, don't heap mental abuse on your much-berated local coal dealer ; the fault does not lie with him, for as a matter of fact the high cost of coal is playing havoc with his business. An investigation into the cause of the Shanghai coal famine by the "North-China Daily News" has brought to light the following factors which contribute to the present coal crisis, namely : the war in China, the drought in Japan and the resultant failure of the Japanese hydro-electric plants, Japanese monopoly of coal produced in China, and the European war.

Before the Sino-Japanese war started in the summer of 1937, local coal merchants were selling their commodity for $16 a ton and were making more money out of the coal business than they are today. This may sound preposterous to irate consumers who are faced with the alternative of forking out the high price demanded for coal today or hibernating for the winter, but it is true. In fact some local dealers are considering deserting the coal trade for the comparatively more secure and lucrative business of selling lawn mowers to the Eskimos.
Most of the coal consumed in Shanghai today is Calcutta coal. This coal, on the docks at Calcutta, costs importers about $36.50 a ton, yet when it is landed in Shanghai it has reached the amazing price of $212 a ton, not including the dealer's profit. The answer is obvious; the high cost of freighting the coal from India to Shanghai is responsible for the terrific price demanded here. Ironically enough China is capable of producing enough coal to fill the demands of practically the entire Far East, but what little coal is being produced in this country now is practically completely monopolized by the Japanese.

Drought In Japan
The continuous drought in Japan which has paralyzed the Japanese hydro-electric system has created an enormous demand for fuel to operate the power plants. Japanese mines, producing only a little over 40,000,000 tons of coal each year, cannot meet this demand and consequently the country is forced to import coal. Practically all the coal mined in the Japanese occupied areas in China is shipped direct to Japan, with a limited quantity being shipped to Shanghai by the Kailan Mining Administration. This coal has been rationed out most fairly among the old customers of the K.M.A. and at a reasonable price.
Even the coal which Japan obtains from China cannot fulfill the country's needs, however, and she is also forced to turn to Indian markets for the fuel. Most of the mines which are in Japanese controlled territory in China have been destroyed, railways which formerly carried the mineral from the mines to the coast have been torn up, and what little coal can be mined after makeshift repairs goes to feed the railway engines of the Japanese military trains. Ironically enough, Japan was able to import more coal from China before the war started than she is today.

War In Europe
The war in Europe contributes to the high price of coal in Shanghai in that the war caused a world-wide increase in shipping rates. Before September 3 the price of Indian coal, landed in Shanghai, was roughly $64 a ton. At that time the time charter rate of shipping was nine shillings a dead-weight ton but now that rate has risen to 22 shillings and added to the fact that it takes about 50 days to make a round trip from Shanghai to Calcutta the freight price on one ton of coal has increased to the present abnormal figure of $145.
The coal actually costs about $36.50 a ton in Calcutta and this, added to the $145 required for freighting each ton of coal, plus $6.50 importer's commission, $6 customs duty in Shanghai, $3.50 landing charge, $8 lost weight and $6 delivery charge makes a ton of coal cost the dealer $212, delivered to his coal yard. Of course the coal dealer is not in the business entirely for his health and he tacks on about 5 per cent. for his modest share, which brings the total to over $220, the sum the consumer has to pay for coal when it finally reaches him.
But it will not remain long at this price. It is significant to note that during the Great War shipping rates rose as high as 52 shillings a dead-weight ton, which is over twice as high as the present figure of 22 shillings, and shipping men believe that rates will climb as high as they were during the last war.
If the war in China ceased, the price of coal, in time, would have a substantial decline because the short distance over which the coal would be freighted would have a negative effect on the shipping rate. For example, it takes 50 days to bring a cargo of coal from Calcutta to Shanghai but a cargo from some China port, such as Tsingtao, could reach Shanghai in three days. Even if the China war did come to a halt, experts figure that it would take fully a year before sufficient coal could be brought to Shanghai to remedy the situation.
The type of coal which has been dealt with up to now is soft coal. Anthracite, or hard coal, is being imported to Shanghai from Indo-China and is selling on the local market for $180 a ton. Coal dealers predict that the price of hard coal will reach the same heights as that of soft coal in a few months as it is doubtful whether or not Indo-China can continue to meet Shanghai demands.

Inspite of the high cost there has been a terrific demand for soft coal in Shanghai. Practically every factory in Shanghai is equipped to burn only soft coal and as long as industry keeps booming there will be a demand for fuel. Biggest consumer of coal in Shanghai is the Shanghai Power Company, whose power plants eat up almost 700,000 tons of coal each year. By agreement with the K.M.A. the power company obtains 300,000 tons from that firm at something like $46 a ton, but the balance, almost 400,000 tons, must be obtained elsewhere at local market prices. The S.P.C. has contracted for coal up to June of this year, but if the price rises higher after that period, the rates for bulk power supply will necessarily increase also.
As far as local merchants are concerned, dealing in coal these days is a risky business, and the dealer has to take all of that risk. A dealer has to advance about $800,000 to order a shipload of coal from Calcutta. Naturally it takes time to place the order and charter a ship and by the time the coal is on its way to Shanghai, hostilities in China may cease, thus causing a sudden psychological drop in the price of the commodity, and the dealer would have to sell out at a loss.

Things Look Black
Indeed, things continue to look black in the coal industry, and that's no pun either. At least as long as the Calcutta market remains open Shanghai will be able to get coal, whatever the price, but it will be recalled that during the Great War there was a government ban on the export of coal from India. The price of coal in India has not increased much since the war began, but there have been no demands upon Indian industry similar to those of the Great War, and if there should be a call for India to expand her manufacturing facilities, it might result in the shutting off of India as a source of coal. Even now, local coal merchants are studying ways and means of importing coal from the United States at a price which would meet the present cost of Calcutta coal.
There is a certain bitter irony about importing coal to China when one realizes the amazing mineral wealth of this country. In certain provinces railways are laid on beds of coal while in others whole stretches of highways are cut through seams of coal and the excess material thrown up in piles for miles along the road, to lie untouched. Truly a case of carrying coals to Newcastle.

1940年2月14日

上海煤炭形势
前景黯淡

高昂运费导致成本异常飙升；经销商利润微薄

《字林西报》专讯

就煤炭而言，上海目前的处境十分糟糕，这种珍贵商品在市场上的售价高达令人难以置信的每吨220美元。而且未来也看不到缓解的迹象，因为煤炭价格正逐周稳步攀升。现在，请不要把精神上的谩骂倾泻在你那备受指责的本地煤商身上；过错并不在他，因为事实上，高昂的煤炭成本正在严重破坏他的生意。《字林西报》对上海煤荒原因进行的调查揭示了导致当前煤炭危机的以下因素，即：中国战事、日本干旱及其导致的水力发电厂停产、日本对中国产煤炭的垄断，以及欧洲战争。

在1937年夏季中日战争爆发之前，本地煤商以每吨16美元的价格出售他们的商品，并且从煤炭业务中赚取的利润比今天还要多。这对于那些面临要么支付今天高昂的煤价、要么挨过整个冬天的愤怒消费者来说，听起来可能荒谬绝伦，但这却是事实。事实上，一些本地经销商正在考虑放弃煤炭贸易，转而从事相对更安全且有利可图的向爱斯基摩人出售割草机的业务。

目前上海消费的大部分煤炭是加尔各答煤炭。这种煤炭在加尔各答码头的成本约为每吨36.50美元，但当它运抵上海时，价格已涨至惊人的每吨212美元，这还不包括经销商的利润。答案显而易见；从印度到上海的高昂煤炭运输费用导致了此处索要的天价。具有讽刺意味的是，中国有能力生产足够的煤炭来满足几乎整个远东的需求，但目前该国生产的少量煤炭实际上几乎完全被日本人垄断。

日本干旱

日本持续的干旱使日本水力发电系统陷入瘫痪，从而产生了巨大的燃料需求以运行发电厂。日本煤矿每年仅生产略超过4,000万吨煤炭，无法满足这一需求，因此该国被迫进口煤炭。在中国日军占领区开采的几乎所有煤炭都直接运往日本，只有有限数量的煤炭由开滦矿务总局（Kailan Mining Administration）运往上海。这些煤炭已在开滦矿务总局的老客户中以相当公平的方式进行了配给，且价格合理。

然而，即使是从中国获得的煤炭也无法满足日本的需求，该国也被迫转向印度市场寻求燃料。位于中国日军控制区内的大多数煤矿已被摧毁，以前将矿产从矿山运往沿海的铁路已被拆除，经过临时修复后能开采的少量煤炭都用于供给日本军用列车的火车头。具有讽刺意味的是，日本在战前能从中国进口的煤炭比现在还要多。

欧洲战争

欧洲战争导致上海煤炭价格高企，因为这场战争引起了全球航运费率的上涨。在9月3日之前，运抵上海的印度煤炭价格约为每吨64美元。当时的船舶期租费率为每载重吨9先令，但现在该费率已升至22先令，加上从上海到加尔各答往返一次大约需要50天这一事实，每吨煤炭的运费已增加到目前异常的145美元。

煤炭在加尔各答的实际成本约为每吨36.50美元，加上每吨煤炭所需的145美元运费，再加上6.50美元的进口商佣金、6美元的上海关税、3.50美元的卸货费、8美元的损耗重量以及6美元的送货费，使得每吨煤炭到达经销商煤场时的成本为212美元。当然，煤炭经销商做生意并非为了健康，他加上了约5%的微薄利润，这使得总额超过220美元，即消费者最终获得煤炭时必须支付的金额。

但这一价格不会维持太久。值得注意的是，在第一次世界大战期间，航运费率曾高达每载重吨52先令，是目前22先令水平的两倍多，航运界人士认为费率将攀升至上次战争期间的水平。

如果中国战事停止，煤炭价格假以时日将会大幅下降，因为煤炭运输距离缩短将对航运费率产生负面影响。例如，从加尔各答将一船煤炭运到上海需要50天，但从中国某个港口（如青岛）出发的货物只需三天即可抵达上海。即使中国战事真的停止，专家估计也需要整整一年时间才能将足够的煤炭运到上海以扭转局势。

迄今为止所涉及的煤炭类型是烟煤（软煤）。无烟煤（硬煤）正从法属印度支那进口到上海，在当地市场的售价为每吨180美元。煤炭经销商预测，几个月内硬煤的价格将达到与烟煤相同的高位，因为法属印度支那能否继续满足上海的需求尚存疑问。

尽管成本高昂，上海对烟煤的需求依然巨大。上海几乎每家工厂都只配备燃烧烟煤的设备，只要工业保持繁荣，对燃料的需求就会存在。上海最大的煤炭消费者是上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company），其发电厂每年消耗近70万吨煤炭。根据与开滦矿务总局的协议，电力公司以约每吨46美元的价格从该公司获得30万吨煤炭，但剩余的近40万吨必须以当地市场价格从其他地方获取。上海电力公司已签订合同购买煤炭直至今年六月，但如果此后价格上涨，批量电力供应费率必然也会随之增加。

就本地商人而言，如今经营煤炭是一项高风险业务，经销商必须承担所有风险。经销商必须预付约80万美元才能从加尔各答订购一船煤炭。自然，下单和租船需要时间，而当煤炭运往上海途中时，中国境内的敌对行动可能会停止，从而导致该商品价格突然因心理因素下跌，经销商将被迫亏本抛售。

形势严峻

的确，煤炭行业的形势持续严峻，这并非双关语。至少只要加尔各答市场保持开放，无论价格如何，上海都能获得煤炭，但人们应记得，在第一次世界大战期间，政府曾禁止从印度出口煤炭。自战争爆发以来，印度的煤炭价格并未大幅上涨，但印度工业并未面临类似第一次世界大战期间的需求，如果要求印度扩大其制造设施，可能会导致切断印度作为煤炭来源地的局面。即便现在，本地煤商也在研究以符合当前加尔各答煤炭成本的价格从美国进口煤炭的方法。

当人们意识到这个国家惊人的矿产财富时，向中国进口煤炭存在着某种苦涩的讽刺意味。在某些省份，铁路铺设在煤层之上，而在其他省份，整段公路切开煤层，多余的物料堆积在道路旁数英里处，无人问津。这真是典型的“把煤运到纽卡斯尔”（多此一举）。

FEB 1 4 1940

Coal Prices In Shanghai May Climb Above
Record High Reached During World War

Coal prices may soar beyond the $350-per-ton mark, the record high reached during the last World War, in the near future if the existing rate of increases keeps its present pace, a leading coal dealer told THE CHINA PRESS yesterday. He revealed that the city was facing the most acute shortage since the 1914 hostilities.

From quotations which range from $100 to $110 per ton obtained about three months ago, soft coal has gone up to nearly $180 per ton during the Chinese New Year holidays. Since no improvement in the market condition was in sight, the prices were expected to reach beyond $200 per ton within the next few weeks.

Even coal briquettes, coal generally used by the small eating places and in workingmen's homes, were quoted at as high as $100 per ton. Similar increases had been noted in the prices of anthracite during the past three months, the present quotations having been set at about $140 per ton of Hongay Coal.

Cause Cited

Causes responsible for the increases in prices were listed as follow:
1. Shantung and Keelung coal, formerly supplying about 20 per cent of the city's needs, having been diverted to Japan due to an acute shortage there.
2. Mounting freight charges as the number of bottoms available for shipments of coal to Shanghai diminishes due to war conditions in Europe and Asia.
3. Shortage of coal in India, whose production having been diverted Europe to supply the fuel requirements of the Allied Powers.
4. Phenomenal declines in the exchange value of the Chinese dollar.

Shortage Predicted

Immediately before the outbreak of the European War, when Indian coal could still be obtained at about $50 per ton in Shanghai, the coal dealer stated, the present shortage was predicted but no attempt was made by responsible quarters here to check what was generally considered inevitable.

While little doubt was expressed that the shortage was due partly to war conditions all over the world and to the drop in the exchange value of the Chinese dollar, the principal cause of the present state of affairs was said to be due to the shortage in Japan which in late months had been draining on the production of Formosa as well as Shantung.

It was pointed out that however short shipping facilities might be the present shortage here would not obtain if shipments from North China and Formosa continued to reach Shanghai at the former rate. Coal from those areas was considered more fit for the Shanghai market since their prices were comparatively lower than supplies from abroad.

Many Ships Chartered

Regarding shipping facilities, the dealer revealed that some large consumers had been forced to charter more vessels for their own use in order to bring their required supplies to Shanghai from the production areas, especially from abroad.

Asked whether the coal consumption here would diminish as the winter months come to a close, the dealer stated that the amount actually required here remained essentially the same each month of the year.

While it is true that with the return of spring and summer, houses no longer need to be heated, it was stated, the amount of fuel required in the production of power and other uses increased in about the same proportion. The monthly coal requirement here, he said, amounts to about 80,000 tons in all.

Of this amount, the Kailan Mining Administration supplied about half, shipping it from their own mines in the North on their chartered bottoms. The other million tons were brought here by large coal users including the Shanghai Power Company and by other distributors.

1940年2月14日

上海煤价可能攀升至
超过第一次世界大战期间创下的历史高点

一位主要煤炭经销商昨日告诉《大美晚报》，如果现有的涨幅保持目前的速度，煤炭价格在不久的将来可能会飙升至每吨350美元以上，超过上次世界大战期间创下的历史最高纪录。他透露，上海正面临自1914年战事以来最严重的短缺。

软煤价格从大约三个月前获得的每吨100至110美元的报价，在春节期间已涨至接近每吨180美元。由于市场状况未见改善迹象，预计未来几周内价格将突破每吨200美元。

即使是小餐馆和工人家庭通常使用的煤球，报价也高达每吨100美元。在过去三个月中，无烟煤价格也出现了类似的上涨，目前红芽煤（Hongay Coal）的报价定为每吨约140美元。

 cited 原因

导致价格上涨的原因列举如下：
1. 山东和基隆煤炭，以前供应城市约20%的需求，由于日本严重短缺而被转运至日本。
2. 随着可用于向上海运输煤炭的船只数量因欧洲和亚洲的战事而减少，运费不断上涨。
3. 印度煤炭短缺，其产量被转移至欧洲以供应盟国的燃料需求。
4. 中国货币汇率急剧下跌。

预测短缺

这位煤炭经销商表示，就在欧洲战争爆发前夕，当时在上海仍能以约每吨50美元的价格获得印度煤炭，人们就预测到了当前的短缺，但本地有关责任方并未试图阻止这一普遍被认为不可避免的局面。

虽然很少有人怀疑短缺部分是由于世界各地的战事和中国货币汇率下跌造成的，但据说造成当前局势的主要原因是日本的短缺，日本在最近几个月一直耗尽台湾以及山东的产量。

有人指出，无论航运设施多么短缺，如果来自华北和台湾的 shipments 继续以以前的速度抵达上海，这里的当前短缺就不会发生。来自这些地区的煤炭被认为更适合上海市场，因为它们的价格相对低于国外供应品。

租用多艘船只

关于航运设施，该经销商透露，一些大型消费者被迫租用更多船只供自己使用，以便将所需物资从产区，特别是从国外运到上海。

当被问及随着冬季月份结束，这里的煤炭消耗量是否会减少时，该经销商表示，这里每月实际需要的数量基本上保持不变。

虽然随着春夏季的回归，房屋不再需要供暖，这是事实，但据说，电力生产和其他用途所需的燃料量也以大致相同的比例增加。他说，这里每月的煤炭需求量总计约为8万吨。

在这一数量中，开滦矿务总局供应了大约一半，通过其租用的船只从其北方的自有矿山发货。其余的一百万吨由包括上海电力公司在内的大型煤炭用户以及其他分销商运抵此处。

page_data.en:
FEB 2 8 1940

S.M.C. Asked to
Curb Coal Prices

Freight Reduction Stated
To Be First Necessity in
Letter to Council

The Shanghai Municipal Council
has now been officially approached
by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
here for reducing the price of coal
which affects prices of many other
commodities. A letter has been for-
warded to the Council by the Cham-
ber in which the former is asked to
hold a meeting of managers of ship-
ping firms with a view to first reduc-
ing the freight of coal.
Inquiries at the Chinese Chamber
revealed yesterday that the letter had
not yet brought any reply but it was
said that the business was an urgent
one. A Chamber official stated that
his organization could not tackle with
the problem primarily for the reason
that all shipping firms here are
foreign-owned.
In the Chamber's letter, it is ex-
plained that the raw material needed
for making coal balls used by every
Chinese family here for cooking comes
from mines in Annam. Shanghai
needs about 1,000 tons of such coal
daily. The coal has been transported
here via Haiphong by boats. Since
the freight has been increased the
price of coal is also affected.
As a result of repeated negotiations
between the Chamber and coal
merchants, it has been decided that
the Council should be petitioned for
holding a meeting with shipping
interests for reducing the transporta-
tion fee. By doing so, it is stated,
coal ball manufacturers here may be
able to produce more goods cheaper.
page_data.zh:
1940年2月8日

要求工部局
抑制煤价

致工部局函件称
降低运费为首要之务

上海公共租界工部局
现已正式收到本地中华总商会
关于降低煤价的请求，煤价影响
着许多其他商品的价格。商会已
向工部局递交了一封信函，请其
召集轮船公司经理举行会议，以
期首先降低煤炭运费。
昨日在中华总商会的查询显示，
该信函尚未得到任何回复，但据
称此事紧急。一位商会官员表示，
其组织无法主要着手解决此问题，
原因在于本地的所有轮船公司均
为外商所有。
商会在信中解释说，本地每户中
国家庭烹饪所用的煤球制造所需
原料来自安南（Annam）的煤矿。
上海每日需要此类煤炭约1,000
吨。这些煤炭一直通过船只经海
防（Haiphong）运抵此处。由于
运费上涨，煤价也受到影响。
经过商会与煤商之间的反复谈判，
决定 petition 工部局，要求其与
航运界举行会议以降低运输费用。
据称，这样做可以使本地的煤球
制造商以更低的成本生产更多产
品。

Ta Mei Wan Pao of February 20 :-

Two Coal Hongs In Settlement Found To Be Hoarding

It has been ascertained that a certain big
coal company on Kiangse Road is hoarding some 5,000 to 6,000
tons of coal dust at each of its two yards in Pootung and on
this side of the Whangpoo River. This coal dust is used in the
manufacture of coal briquettes. Another large coal hong
with offices in the International Dispensary Building is
likewise hoarding in its yard in Pootung several thousand

Mr. Yu Ya-ching has requested all these companies to sell

page_data.en:
February, 21, 1940.
Afternoon Translation

Ta Mei Pao :-

SHORTAGE OF COAL IN SHANGHAI DUE TO JAPANESE CONTROL

Owing to the shortage of coal, the Japanese
military authorities are enforcing a control of coal. It
is said that all Japanese commercial concerns have been
ordered not to transport coal from the occupied areas into
the Foreign Settlements in Shanghai and that offenders will
be liable to heavy punishments.
It is learned that all the coal yards located
outside the Foreign Settlements have been instructed to hand
over their coal to the Japanese army. If the Japanese army
has a surplus from their requirements, it will sell a portion
to the Japanese commercial and industrial concerns and only
when the Japanese commercial concerns have a surplus, may the
residents of the Foreign Settlements hope to share in the
supplies.
According to another report, the Japanese army
on Monday detained 500 tons of coal valued at $70,000 destined
for the Foreign Settlements.
At present the coal dumped at a certain
Japanese company has reached a height of 30 feet. This coal
will be for the sole use of the Japanese army.

FILE

下午译文

《大美报》：-

上海煤炭短缺系因日本控制所致

由于煤炭短缺，日本军方当局正
在实施煤炭管制。据悉，所有日
本商行已被命令不得将占领区的
煤炭运入上海的外国租界，违者
将受到严厉惩罚。
据了解，位于外国租界之外的所
有煤栈均已接到指令，将其煤炭
移交给日军。如果日军在满足自
身需求后有剩余，会将部分煤炭
出售给日本工商业机构，只有当
日本商行有剩余时，外国租界的
居民才有希望分享供应。
据另一则报道，日军于周一扣留
了运往外国租界的500吨煤炭，
价值70,000美元。
目前，倾倒在某家日本公司的煤
炭堆积高度已达30英尺。这些煤
炭将专供日军使用。

归档

page_data.en:
February 18, 1940. Morning Translation.

National Herald, Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao,
Shun Pao:

OPEN LETTER ISSUED BY CITIZENS' FEDERATION

The Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation yesterday issued the following letter to the
Nee Tai Shing & Co. (義泰兴) and six other coal briquette
factories:-
"According to a notice published in newspapers by
your factories, more than 20,000 tons of coal briquettes
ordered have not yet been called for and the concerns
making such orders are requested to take delivery of them
as soon as possible.
"This evidently shows that certain persons are
profiteering by hoarding such coal briquettes. We deeply
respect your action in urging the delivery of goods, out of
consideration for the livelihood of the people.
"Lest the livelihood of the people should be
seriously affected in view of the considerable rise in the
price of coal supplies, we hereby request your factories to
urge your clients to deliver the goods at an appointed date,
and if they fail to do so, the goods should be sold at the
cost price, after which the deposits paid by your clients
should be refunded."

Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao publishes the following article to-day :-

GODOWN WARRANTS

A liquidation of the godown warrants for
coal briquettes has now brought about a reduction in the
price of such goods. It is due to the increase in the number
of godown warrants that the price of rice has become
surprisingly high. There are many warrants for rice stored

take rigid measures to press holders of such warrants to
dispose of their stocks at the price limit. This action will
naturally bring about a reduction in the price of rice.

19 2 40

DAILY NEWS

FEB 1 7 1940

Hot Water Shops Hit By
Coal Situation

Chinese Newspapers Urge
Action By Authorities

Chinese press reports and comments strongly urge that foreign authorities in Shanghai should immediately take appropriate actions to cope with the extremely serious situation existing in the coal market.

It is stated that the increase of prices of coal has affected prices of numerous other commodities and businesses, its immediate bad effect being felt by several hundred boiled water supplying shops in foreign areas where the Chinese in general obtain their daily quota of drinking water. Some public-spirited coal shop managers sold small quantities of coal to these small shops. Many such shops, which were recently forced to close business, were reported to be reopening for business but it was said that it was apparent that the supply of coal was too limited to keep their business going.

One report points out there is ample ready stocks of coal in Shanghai. There are about 520,000 tons of coal stored in various godowns here including 60,000 tons of coal especially for making coal balls for cooking purposes. The Settlement authorities are urged to negotiate with coal firms requiring them to sell their cargo.

Definite signs of hoarding were noticed in an advertisement published by several coal ball manufacturing factories asking their customers to remove the big quantities of cargo they bought some time ago. It was pointed out that should they fail to take out their coal balls business contracts would be nullified and money returned. One commentator pointed out that about 20,000 tons of coal balls were thus bought by hoarding customers awaiting high prices.

19 2 40
page_data.zh:
7555/3
1940年2月19日

《每日新闻》

1940年2月17日

热水店受
煤炭局势冲击

中文报纸呼吁
当局采取行动

中文报刊的报道和评论强烈敦促
上海的外国当局立即采取适当行
动，以应对煤炭市场存在的极其
严峻的局势。

据说，煤炭价格的上涨影响了众
多其他商品和商业的价格，其直
接的不良影响波及了外国区域的
数百家热水供应店，一般中国民

额。一些具有公益心的煤店经理
向这些小店铺出售少量煤炭。据

一份报告指出，上海有充足的现

几家煤球制造厂刊登的一则广告

1940年2月19日

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.

COAL PRICES STILL
CAUSING ALARM

Hot Water Shops Hard
Hit By Increases
This Winter

Fantastic coal prices are virtually
creating a panic among local peo-
ple who are connected directly or
indirectly with the use of that
essential material.

One of the first trades affected
by the high price is the coastal
shipping business. To cover the
increased cost of operation on the
part of ship companies, a drastic
rise in interport freight rates was
said to be imminent. In fact, the
overseas freight rates have already
been increased, which was one con-
tributing factor to the present
runaway coal prices. As the coal
output in North China is now very
limited, Shanghai must depend for
its coal supply upon foreign im-
portation. In other words, local
coal prices are at the mercy of
foreign exchange and overseas
freight rates.

The worst victims of the abnormal
coal prices are the local hot water
shops, which provide Shanghai's
masses with hot or boiled water.
Out of the 300-odd shops, over 200
have been forced to close their
business through the hopeless
situation. These shut-downs, how-
ever, succeeded in reviving busi-
ness yesterday, after the three
leading coal trusts agreed to supply
the trade with 600 tons of slack
coal, valued at $170 a ton, at the
special co-operative price of $98
a ton. This amount, however, will
only last a week or so, so that the
hot-water trade is still feeling deep
concern over the future.

It is now believed that drastic
increases in the rates of electricity,
gas, etc. will be a matter of time,
and price advances in restaurants
and bathing-houses, are also in-
evitable. Total stores of coal for
Shanghai are estimated to be around
510,000 tons. Figuring the normal
daily consumption at 2,800 tons,
there should be no cause for alarm.

Meanwhile, coal prices continued
to soar every hour, with briquet-
tes selling at the astounding high
of $6.80 per 100 catties yesterday.
General sentiment looks for a much
higher level than the present rate
of $210 per ton for Kailan lumps,
although this is already a threefold
increase as compared to the price
of $70 per ton only three months
ago. Kailan lumps sold for only
$12 a ton in 1937.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。

煤价仍
引起恐慌

今冬热水店
受涨价重创

荒谬的煤价实际上在直接与间接
使用这种必需材料的本地民众中
造成了恐慌。

受高价影响的首批行业之一是沿
海航运业。据说，为了弥补轮船
公司运营成本的增加，港口间运
费的急剧上涨迫在眉睫。事实上，
海外运费已经上涨，这是导致目
前煤价失控的因素之一。由于华
北的煤炭产量现在非常有限，上
海必须依赖进口来满足煤炭供应。
换句话说，本地煤价受制于外汇
和海外运费。

异常煤价的最大受害者是本地热
水店，这些店铺为上海大众提供
热水或开水。在300多家店铺中，
有200多家因局势无望而被迫停
业。然而，在三家主要煤炭托拉
斯同意以每吨98美元的特别合作
价格，向该行业供应价值每吨170
美元的600吨碎煤后，这些停业
店铺于昨日成功恢复了营业。然
而，这批煤炭仅能维持一周左右，
因此热水行业仍对未来深感担忧。

现在人们认为，电费、煤气费等
的大幅上涨只是时间问题，餐馆
和浴室的价格上涨也是不可避免
的。估计上海的煤炭总储量约为
510,000吨。按每日正常消耗量
2,800吨计算，本不应引起恐慌。

与此同时，煤价每小时都在飙升，
昨天煤球的售价高达每百斤6.80
美元的惊人高位。普遍情绪认为，
开滦块煤的价格水平将远高于目
前的每吨210美元，尽管这已是三
个月前每吨70美元价格的三倍。
1937年，开滦块煤的售价仅为每
吨12美元。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
FEB 1 7 1940

Price Of Soft
Coal Reaches
$280 Per Ton

Gloom pervaded the view-
point of soft coal dealers here
yesterday with announcement
that Calcutta bituminous had
shot up $60 in a week to $280
a ton and was practically im-
possible to get at that.

The Hongay hard coal dealers
were more cheerful, boasting
that their Indo-China product
had held the comparatively
steady level of from $130 and
$140 a ton throughout the first
two weeks of February.

The future of both hard and soft
varieties of the fuel depended on
two factors: exchange of the Chin-
ese dollar and freight rates, it was
stated.

The first was showing definite
tendencies of slipping and the
second, of going up.

In a period of two months the
rate per ton from Calcutta to
Shanghai had advanced from $30 to
$180. Similar rates from Hongay
to Shanghai have advanced from
about $15 to $80 per ton during
the course of the present European
war.

The outlook for Shanghai In-
dustry was definitely pessimistic.
A well-known dealer yesterday
foreboded the shutting down of
several factories and did not
at all discount a prediction
made in the pages of THE
CHINA PRESS several days ago
that coal would continue its
advance from $280 to $350 a ton.
Hongay officials granted that
the local soft coal situation was
bad but insisted their own posi-
tion was "quite normal."

In the meantime veritable moun-
tains of coal have been observed
recently lying along the wharves of
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. Inquiry
yesterday revealed that much of
this is destined for consumption in
Japanese warships with the rest
going to Japanese firms both here
and throughout the Yangtse River
valley.

By a Japanese law of several
months back, this fuel cannot be
sold to foreign firms unless there is
a surplus—which it seems, there
never is.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》（China Press）。
1940年2月17日

软煤价格
达到
每吨280美元

昨日，本地软煤经销商的观点
笼罩在阴郁之中，宣布加尔各答
烟煤在一周内上涨了60美元，达
到每吨280美元，且在这个价位
上几乎无法买到。

鸿基（Hongay）硬煤经销商则较
为乐观，夸耀其印度支那产品在
2月前两周保持了相对稳定的水
平，价格在每吨130至140美元之
间。

据说，这两种燃料（硬煤和软煤）
的未来取决于两个因素：中国货
币的汇率和运费。

前者显示出明确的下滑趋势，而
后者则呈上升趋势。

在两个月期间，从加尔各答到上
海的每吨运费已从30美元上涨至
180美元。在当前欧洲战争期间，
从鸿基到上海的类似运费已从每
吨约15美元上涨至80美元。

上海工业的前景确实悲观。一位
知名经销商昨日预言几家工厂将
关闭，并且完全不排除《大美晚
报》几天前版面中做出的预测，
即煤价将从280美元继续上涨至
每吨350美元。鸿基官员承认本地
软煤形势糟糕，但坚持认为他们
自身的状况“相当正常”。

与此同时，最近观察到三井物产
株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）
的码头上堆积着真正的煤山。昨
日的查询显示，其中大部分 destined
供日本军舰消耗，其余部分则供
应给本地及整个长江流域的日本
公司。

根据几个月前的一项日本法律，
除非有剩余——而这似乎从来都
没有——否则这种燃料不得出售
给外国公司。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JANUARY 28, 1940
Foreign Coal To Help Out
Japanese Shortage
Cabinet Decides On An Emergency Measure In View
Of Difficulties; Industrialists To Give
Their Fullest Possible Support

TOKYO, Jan. 26.—Importation of foreign coal will be allowed as an emergency measure to remedy the shortage of coal and electric power, it was decided by the Cabinet on Tuesday.
It was also announced that the authorities would postpone for the present the invocation of compulsory measures, as coal producers, after lengthy deliberations with the Commerce and Industry Minister, have agreed to increase their deliveries to electric power plants.
This policy was established by the Cabinet after three successive meetings on Monday and Tuesday, as Premier Yonai had requested his colleagues to discuss measures for alleviating the coal shortage immediately, prior to the examination of all other impending questions.
Co-operation Secured
Meanwhile, the Commerce Minister had been negotiating with the representatives of the Mitsui and the Mitsubishi interests, as their support was deemed indispensable for the success of the emergency measures planned by the Government. That support was granted and the Government was able to shelve compulsory measures which it had threatened to take under the Electric Power Regulation Ordinance voted last year by the Diet.
“For the first time in my life, I have humbly bowed in solicitation,” Mr. Ginjiro Fujiwara, Commerce Minister and powerful “paper king” declared to the press. “By this gesture, I have secured full unconditional support of the coal producers,” he added.
It was understood that 160,000 tons stocked in different parts of Japan would be made available by the owners, while 100,000 tons would be imported from Tsingtao, Formosa, Sakhalin and Manchoukuo. This would make up for the shortage of January and February, while the rainy season, beginning in March, would give more hydro-electric power.

Import Permits
As for the imports of foreign coal, which would supplement imports from Japan’s possessions on the continent, necessary permits would be given by the Finance Minister according to the regulations of the exchange control.
All these measures have been supplemented by provisional, drastic steps to offset the shortage of coal to the electric power generating industry. The “Kokumin” reports that large consumers of power were requested to appear at the Metropolitan Police Board on Sunday, to be informed of a plan to institute one or two full holidays before the end of this month.
Under this plan, ordinary industries will close down for two days and munitions industries for one day.
These measures have been found necessary as restrictions which had been decided in the amount of electricity to be used by large consumers had not been observed, according to the statement of Mr. Jiro Masuda, President of the Japan Electric Generating and Transmission Company, in the “Asahi.”
Restrictions Fixed
The restrictions had been fixed at 10 per cent. in the Kwansai (Osaka and region), up to January 14, when it was increased to 28 per cent. and at 10 per cent. in the Kwanto (Tokyo and region) up to January 16 when it was increased to 20 per cent.
The delicate situation inherited from the preceding cabinet in this matter will thus be satisfactorily remedied, it is believed. That situation may be judged by the fact that, due to shortage of electric power, several large factories in the Kwansai had been forced to close down in the middle of this month, including the Dai Nippon Cotton Spinning Company, the plant of the Takeda Pharmaceutical Company and a factory of the Itami Carpet Weaving Company, while several power stations in the Nagoya region have also ceased work.—Havas.

《上海星期日泰晤士报》，1940年1月28日
外国煤炭将助解
日本短缺困境
内阁鉴于困难决定采取紧急措施；工业界将给予全力支持

东京，1月26日电。——内阁于周二决定，允许进口外国煤炭作为紧急措施，以补救煤炭和电力短缺。
当局还宣布，目前暂缓实施强制措施，因为煤炭生产商在与工商大臣进行长时间磋商后，已同意增加对发电厂的供应量。
这一政策是内阁在周一和周二连续召开三次会议后制定的，因为米内（Yonai）首相要求同僚在审议所有其他迫在眉睫的问题之前，立即讨论缓解煤炭短缺的措施。
获得合作
与此同时，工商大臣一直在与三井和三菱财团的代表进行谈判，因为他们的支持被视为政府计划的紧急措施取得成功所不可或缺的。这些支持已获提供，政府因此得以搁置其曾威胁要依据去年帝国议会通过的《电力管理法》采取的强制措施。
“在我一生中，我首次卑躬屈膝地恳求，”工商大臣兼权势显赫的“纸业大王”藤原银次郎先生向新闻界宣称。“通过这一姿态，我获得了煤炭生产商的全面无条件支持，”他补充道。
据悉，储存在日本各地的16万吨煤炭将由业主提供，另有10万吨将从青岛、台湾、库页岛和满洲国进口。这将弥补一月和二月的短缺，而始于三月雨季将带来更多的水力发电。

进口许可证
至于将补充从日本大陆属地进口的外国煤炭进口，财务大臣将根据外汇管制规定颁发必要的许可证。
所有这些措施都辅以临时的严厉步骤，以抵消发电行业的煤炭短缺。据《国民新闻》报道，大型电力用户被要求于周日前往警视厅，获悉一项在本月底前实行一两天全休假的计划。
根据该计划，普通工业将停工两天，军需工业将停工一天。
据日本发电送电公司总裁增田次郎先生在《朝日新闻》上的声明，由于此前决定的针对大型用户的用电量限制未被遵守，这些措施被认为是必要的。
限制确定
关西地区（大阪及周边地区）的限制定为10%，直至1月14日，随后增至28%；关东地区（东京及周边地区）的限制定为10%，直至1月16日，随后增至20%。
人们相信，前任内阁在此问题上遗留的微妙局势将由此得到令人满意的补救。从以下事实可以判断当时的局势：由于电力短缺，关西地区的几家大工厂在本月中旬被迫关闭，包括大日本棉纺株式会社、武田制药厂的工厂以及尼崎地毯织造厂的一家工厂，而名古屋地区的几个发电站也停止了工作。——哈瓦斯社。

CHINA PRESS.
DEC 1 3 1939
Coal Dealer
Increase In
Freight Said
Hiking Prices

Coal, hard and soft, will ad-
vance in price considerably here
in the near future in the view
of big local dealers. This
situation, they say, is coming
about largely because of higher
freight rates and not due to any
particular shortage of present
stocks.

Hard coal at present fetches $108
a ton at the cheapest Shanghai
dealers. It is expected to advance
to a round $126, a price at which
some merchants are even now sell-
ing. Soft coal from North China
brings $40 a ton now, an increase
of $6 over last month's price. Soft
coal from India sells locally for
$112 a ton.

Higher freight rates from mining
centers are given by most dealers
as the excuse for the jump in
prices. Another reason is the drop
in the value of the Chinese dollar.

Freightage Soars

Freight rates from Indo-
China have increased from
about $20 a ton in August to
$32 today. A North China com-
pany reported yesterday that it
had been able to keep prices to
a minimum because many of
its ships were on a charter basis
when the European war started.
Three of them, however, were
taken from the firm last month
for war service and vessels
chartered in their place cost
more.

As long as the remaining
early charters hold out the com-
pany can furnish Shanghai with
$40 a ton soft coal. When new
ships replace them the price will
automatically advance.

An interesting feature of the
situation is that coal consumption
in the city has remained almost
normal, according to all dealers.
This fact holds true of both the
high grade coal and briquettes used
by the poorer portions of the
population. The phenomenon may
be attributed partly to the increas-
ed number of dwellings, residences
and industrial buildings constructed
during the past few months.

K.M.A. Imports

The Kailan Mining Administra-
tion expects to increase its Dec-
ember imports to Shanghai by
10,000 tons over the November
figure. Most of this however, will
go to local factories which even
with this addition are reported to
fear a shortage some time this
winter.

There was a diversity of opinion
among coal dealers yesterday as to
the reason for the freight rate in-
creases. The natural advance in
prices brought on by war was the
most outstanding cause suggested,
although all admitted that there
are plenty of steamers in the Far
East.

One importer of hard coal declar-
ed that some of the ships he
chartered formerly were getting
better rates now for carrying
Saigon rice, and coal merchants
were consequently forced to in-
crease their offers

（印：S. E. REC. 7555）

《字林西报》
1939年12月13日
煤商称
运费上涨
导致提价

本地大经销商认为，近期这里的硬煤和软煤价格将大幅上涨。他们说，这种情况的出现主要是因为运费较高，而非由于当前库存特别短缺。

目前，上海最便宜的经销商处硬煤售价为每吨108美元。预计价格将涨至整整126美元，一些商人甚至现在就以这个价格出售。华北软煤目前售价为每吨40美元，比上月价格上涨了6美元。印度软煤在本地售价为每吨112美元。

大多数经销商将采矿中心运费上涨作为价格跳涨的借口。另一个原因是中国货币价值的下跌。

运费飙升

从印度支那运来的运费已从8月份的每吨约20美元增加到今天的32美元。一家华北公司昨天报告称，由于欧洲战争爆发时其许多船只处于包租状态，因此能够将价格保持在最低水平。然而，上个月其中三艘船被征用用于战时服务，取而代之的包租船只成本更高。

只要剩余的早期包租合同仍然有效，该公司就能以每吨40美元的价格向上海供应软煤。当新船取代它们时，价格将自动上涨。

据所有经销商称，这种情况的一个有趣特点是，城市的煤炭消费量几乎保持正常。这一事实对于高档煤和贫困人口使用的煤球都适用。这种现象部分可归因于过去几个月建造的房屋、住宅和工业建筑数量增加。

开滦矿务局进口

开滦矿务局预计12月对上海的进口量将比11月增加1万吨。然而，其中大部分将流向本地工厂，据报道，即使有了这一增量，这些工厂仍担心今年冬季某个时候会出现短缺。

昨天，煤商们对运费上涨的原因意见不一。战争带来的自然价格上涨是被提出的最突出原因，尽管所有人都承认远东地区有足够的轮船。

一位硬煤进口商宣称，他以前包租的一些船只现在因运送西贡大米而获得更好的费率，因此煤商被迫提高报价

（印章：S. E. REC. 7555）

26890
$500,000 OF
COAL STOLEN
City-Wide Ring Exposed
As ‘Fence’ Faces Court

KAILAN, POWER COMPANY,
MBK AMONG BIG VICTIMS
OF COAL-THIEF RACKET
Sensational! Exposures Expected

Coal thefts to the value of over $500,000 have been carried out in Shanghai in the past few months and it has not been until today that one single member of a remarkable racket gang could be brought to court. Today an alleged receiver faced the Second Special District Court.

Firms which have been victimized by this ring are the Kailan Mining Administration, Shanghai Power Company, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha (famous for its own robberies of eggs from American and British firms), Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong and one or two smaller concerns importing coal into Shanghai.

Stolen Coal Sold
Altogether eight suspects have so far been rounded-up, but seven of them are believed to be small fry, concerned only with the actual thefts of coal from various places, and not with the distribution of the stolen article. No less than 8000 tons of coal have been stolen in the past few months ... and distributed again for sale in Shanghai.

Police investigations in the situation began tightening around leaders of a city-wide racket believed to be supported by some powerful influence, following the arrest of the eight men, one of them believed to be a receiver of the stolen coal property. The receiver, Shu Wei-nan, was brought up before the Second Special District Court this morning by the Customs River Police, and was remanded in custody pending further police investigations which are expected to lead to wholesale arrests of members linked in the racket within the next few days.

（批：10/11/37）
page_data.zh:
26890
价值50万美元的
煤炭被盗
全市性团伙曝光
“销赃者”面临法庭审判

开滦、电力公司、
MBK 成为煤炭盗窃勒索案的重大受害者
预计将有轰动性揭露

过去几个月，上海发生了价值超过50万美元的煤炭盗窃案，直到今天，一个非凡的犯罪团伙中才有一名成员被带上法庭。今天，一名涉嫌销赃者在第二特区法院出庭。

受该团伙侵害的公司包括开滦矿务局、上海电力公司、三井物产株式会社（以其抢劫英美公司鸡蛋而闻名）、尼泰兴煤号以及一两家向上海进口煤炭的小公司。

被盗煤炭被出售
截至目前，共有八名嫌疑人被捕，但其中七人被认为是小角色，仅涉及从各处实际盗窃煤炭，而不涉及被盗物品的分销。在过去几个月里，不少于8000吨煤炭被盗……并在上海重新分销出售。

在逮捕这八人（其中一人被认为是被盗煤炭财产的接收者）之后，警方调查开始收紧围绕一个被认为受到某些强大势力支持的全市性犯罪团伙头目的包围圈。接收者舒伟南（Shu Wei-nan，音译）今天上午由海关水上警察带至第二特区法院，并被还押候审，等待进一步的警方调查，预计这些调查将在未来几天内导致与该团伙有关的成员被大规模逮捕。

（批注：1937年11月10日）

page_data.en:
Retail Shops
The Shanghai Evening Post first learned of the case in August, when information was obtained on the manner in which the stolen coal was being sold by receivers to various Chinese and foreign retail coal shops in all parts of the city, including the French Concession, Shanghai Special Municipality areas, and the International Settlement.
During the past six months prices "marked" by the receivers for selling the stolen coal have been from $20 per ton for cheaper quality coal and up to $50 per ton for superior grades, while retail shops who took the stolen coal continued to maintain selling prices around $100 per ton.

'Good Prospects
Police investigations in the situation have taken a long time, and search is still being made for leaders of the racket. The arrest of the eight suspects by the police are believed to hold good prospects for early elimination of the illegal practices employed against the coal importers.
An official of the Kailan Mining Administration, interviewed by a member of the Evening Post, declared that it was almost impossible to estimate the quantity of coal stolen from the company within the past few months.

Big Imports
He pointed out that the estimated total of coal imported into Shanghai each month is just a little under 200,000 tons. Of this total the KMA receives close to 90,000 tons monthly, importing solely from its mines in North China.
Next highest quantity shipped into Shanghai is that of the Power Company, with approximately 50,-000 tons each month. The Mitsui Bussan Kaisha imports various kinds of coal from Japan, Keelung and Indo-China, totalling, monthly, nearly 30,000 tons, while the Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong imports 20,000 tons of coal from North and South China. About 10,000 tons more are purchased by smaller enterprises.

Steady Losses
It was disclosed to the Evening Post that approximately 1300 tons of coal have been stolen each month from the importing hongs since last May. Of this amount, it was further learned, the KMA has suffered monthly losses averaging 400 tons, Shanghai Power Company 200 tons, MBK 300 tons, and the Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong and smaller firms, a combined total of 400 tons.
Methods followed by those responsible for the coal thefts were bared during investigations carried out by police, and revealed considerable daring on the part of the criminals.

Methods Of Thieves
Following arrival of a coal-ship, usually carrying 4000 tons of coal, nearly the entire cargo of coal is loaded into lighters and taken from various points of the river to the Shanghai side of the waterfront.
Advantage is taken by the coal-robbers while the lighters are berthed during the night, when they succeed in "helping themselves" to as much coal from the moored lighters as their small junks and other craft will hold. After this the marauders retreat to the Yang-ching Creek, situated close to Holt's Wharf on the Pootung side, and under jurisdiction of the Shanghai Special Municipality.

Power Company
The Shanghai Power Company, the investigations disclosed, is a more open "target" for the efforts of the coal-thieves as a result of the large supplies of coal which remain in barges berthed alongside the company's Riverside plant in Yangtzepoo for some time before being unloaded.
In numerous cases where investigations were made following coal thefts from the importing hongs and the SPC, clues indicated that the robbers belonged to the same invariably took the stolen property up Yang-ching Creek.

Distribution
The interesting phase to the wide-scale coal thefts, and the part which has led the authorities to the firm belief that a widespread "ring" is conducting the operations, are "sales" of the stolen property which are transacted by brokers for the receivers and retail coal hongs.
After obtaining a sufficient number of "clients" to take delivery of the stolen coal here, a few cargo junks and other small craft tie up at the Chapoo Road Bridge cargo jetty and then the coal is "delivered"—at $20, or a little more per ton. Afterwards this same coal is sold for around $100 per ton.

Police Baffled
Despite this knowledge, however, the police authorities have been unable to take any action except for frequent arrests of thieves taking part in the robberies, nothing definite could be established against actual receivers or others playing their roles in the coal robberies "behind the scenes," until lately.
Until lately, nothing definite could be established against actual receivers of the stolen property, or others believed to be playing influencing roles in the robberies "behind the scenes."

Honor Among Thieves
Thieves arrested by the police persisted in refusing to divulge the identity of either the brokers or receivers of the stolen, the Evening Post learned regarding investigations carried out during the past few months.
It was known, however, that apart from Chinese hongs accepting the stolen coal at cheap prices, several foreign retail coal shops were also taking part in the purchases.

Vague Replies
Detailed investigations were carried out by police among the various retail coal hongs, when dealers were questioned regarding their stocks. In a few suspicious cases, owners have made vague replies of having purchased their cargo "last winter," or offer similar explanations when questioned.
Although a matter of slow progress owing to various complications hindering negotiations, and end was foreseen in the near future the robberies, the Evening Post learned today, with early arrests of those operating the big racket.

268 3
page_data.zh:
零售商店

《上海晚邮报》（The Shanghai Evening Post）于八月首次获悉此案，当时掌握了关于收赃者如何将被盗煤炭出售给全市各地（包括法租界、上海特别市区域以及公共租界）的中外零售煤店的信息。

在过去六个月中，收赃者为出售被盗煤炭所“标定”的价格，从劣质煤每吨20美元到优质煤每吨50美元不等，而收购这些被盗煤炭的零售店则继续维持每吨约100美元的售价。

前景良好

警方对此情况的调查耗时良久，目前仍在搜寻该犯罪团伙的头目。警方逮捕八名嫌疑人，被认为为早日消除针对煤炭进口商的非法行为带来了良好的前景。

开滦矿务局（Kailan Mining Administration）的一位官员在接受《晚邮报》记者采访时宣称，几乎无法估算过去几个月内从该公司被盗的煤炭数量。

大量进口

他指出，估计每月进口到上海的煤炭总量略低于20万吨。在此总量中，开滦矿务局（KMA）每月接收近9万吨，全部从其华北各煤矿进口。

运抵上海数量次之的是电力公司，每月约50,000吨。三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）从日本、基隆和印度支那进口各类煤炭，每月总计近30,000吨，而义泰兴煤号（Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong）从中国南北方进口20,000吨煤炭。另有约10,000吨由较小的企业购买。

持续损失

据向《晚邮报》披露，自去年五月以来，每月从各进口商号被盗的煤炭约为1300吨。进一步获悉，在此数量中，开滦矿务局（KMA）每月平均损失400吨，上海电力公司损失200吨，三井物产株式会社（MBK）损失300吨，义泰兴煤号及较小商号合计损失400吨。

警方在调查中揭露了盗窃煤炭者所使用的手段，显示罪犯相当大胆。

窃贼手法

运煤船抵达后（通常载有4000吨煤炭），几乎整船煤炭都被装入驳船，并从河流各处运至上海一侧的岸边。

煤炭窃贼利用驳船夜间停泊之机，成功从系泊的驳船上“自行取用”尽可能多的煤炭，装满其小型舢板和其他船只。随后，这些劫掠者撤退至位于浦东霍尔特码头（Holt's Wharf）附近、受上海特别市管辖的洋泾浜（Yang-ching Creek）。

电力公司

调查显示，由于大量煤炭在卸货前需在上海杨树浦（Yangtzepoo）电力公司沿江工厂旁停泊的驳船上存放一段时间，上海电力公司成为煤炭窃贼更容易下手的“目标”。

在对从进口商号和上海电力公司（SPC）盗窃煤炭的多起案件进行调查时，线索表明窃贼属于同一伙人，且总是将赃物沿洋泾浜向上游运走。

分销

大规模煤炭盗窃案中引人关注的环节，也是导致当局坚信有一个广泛的“团伙”在运作的原因，是收赃者和零售煤行通过经纪人进行的赃物“销售”。

在找到足够多的“客户”在此接收被盗煤炭后，几艘货用舢板和其他小型船只停靠在乍浦路桥货栈码头，随后以每吨20美元或稍高的价格“交付”煤炭。此后，同样的煤炭以每吨约100美元的价格售出。

警方受阻

然而，尽管掌握这些情况，警方除频繁逮捕参与抢劫的窃贼外，一直无法采取其他行动；直到最近，仍无法对实际的收赃者或在煤炭抢劫案幕后起作用的其他人确立任何确凿证据。

直到最近，仍无法对被盗财产的实际接收者，或被认为在抢劫案“幕后”发挥影响作用的其他人确立任何确凿证据。

盗亦有道

《晚邮报》获悉，在过去几个月的调查中，被警方逮捕的窃贼坚持拒绝透露被盗物品的经纪人或收赃者的身份。

然而，众所周知，除了以低价接受被盗煤炭的中国商号外，几家外国零售煤店也参与了购买。

含糊其辞

警方在各零售煤行中进行了详细调查，询问经销商关于其库存的情况。在少数可疑案件中，店主在被问及时作出含糊回答，称货物是“去年冬天”购买的，或提供类似的解释。

《晚邮报》今日获悉，尽管由于各种阻碍谈判的复杂因素导致进展缓慢，但随着操纵这一大型犯罪团伙的人员即将被捕，预计这些抢劫案将在不久的将来终结。

NOV 2 · 1939

City Said
Facing No
Coal Famine

Heavy imports from abroad during recent weeks have substantially augmented the coal stock in Shanghai and virtually eliminated any danger of a shortage during the winter months, the Credit Men's Economic Bulletin, quoting fuel market circles, said yesterday.

It was stated that during September imports of coal into Shanghai amounted to 265,000 tons as compared with the 280,000 tons of last month. Most of the imports were said to have originated from India and Japanese ports.

As a result of the increased supply, the market price of the best quality anthracite has been fixed by the Coal Merchants Guild at a maximum of $118 per ton, and first grade Hongay dust at $66 per ton.

The price of coal briquettes was also reported to have declined sharply. Merchants are now retailing the fuel at from $3.10 to $3.20 per picul, as against the price of $3.40 recently fixed by their guild.

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 1 3 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. C. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 73340
Date 13 / 10 39

High Freight Cost, Drop In Dollar’s Value
Send Coal Prices Skyrocketing In Shanghai

City’s Poor Particularly
Affected By Rising
Cost Of Fuel

By PAUL FENG

Sharp declines in the exchange value of the Chinese dollar in late months and rapidly increasing freight charges are responsible for the mounting cost of coal, which in recent weeks hit an all-time high in the city.

This was the consensus of opinion among the city’s leading coal importers and dealers when interviewed by THE CHINA PRESS on the coal situation here.

It was stated that while there was yet no imminent threat that Shanghai would soon face an acute shortage of the fuel, it was revealed that shippers and importers had found it increasingly difficult to secure bottoms to transport their supplies to the city.

City’s Poor Hit

Coal, like rice, it was pointed out, is an indispensable commodity in the average household; therefore, any increase in its cost works serious hardship upon the general public, particularly among the poor whose kitchens consume no less than 100,000 tons of coal a year.

“Consequently,” a dealer emphasized, “when anthracite coal, sold at $37 a ton in September, 1937, jumped to $108 a ton this month wholesale, its far-reaching effects may be readily appreciated.”

In like manner, the price of bituminous coal has skyrocketed. From the $18.50-per-ton wholesale quotation early in 1937, the price climbed to about $70-per-ton in September and had taken another $20 jump since the first of this month.

Gas, Light Rates Hiked

In a no less significant way, the rising cost of coal hit the better-to-do homes which are ordinarily supplied with gas and electricity. It was recalled that public utilities in the past month placed surcharges ranging from 80 to 120 per cent on the consumers’ bills. One of the reasons given for the increases was that coal prices had gone up steadily.

Regarding freight charges for transporting coal to Shanghai, the Hongay Sales Ltd. shortly before the war paid only $2 per ton from Indo-China. At present, the company is paying 10 shillings per ton, or approximately at yesterday’s exchange rate, $27 national currency.

Generally, it was found that other importers, including the Kailan Mining Administration and other leading dealers, had to pay considerable higher freight charges than before. The Hongay Sales Ltd. may be considered typical.

（批：Liu 13/10）

《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）。
1939年10月13日

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. C. 登记处
编号 S. B. D. 73340
日期 1939年10月13日

高昂运费与美元贬值
致使上海煤价飙升

城市贫民尤其
受到燃料成本
上涨的影响

作者：PAUL FENG

近几个月中国元汇兑价值的急剧下跌以及运费的快速上涨，是导致煤炭成本不断攀升的原因，该成本在最近几周内达到了该市的历史最高点。

这是《字林西报》就本地煤炭形势采访本市主要煤炭进口商和经销商时达成的普遍共识。

据称，虽然上海目前尚未面临迫在眉睫的严重燃料短缺威胁，但船运公司和进口商发现，越来越难以 securing bottoms（原文不清，意指租赁船只舱位）将物资运抵本市。

城市贫民受冲击

指出，煤炭如同大米一样，是普通家庭不可或缺的必需品；因此，其成本的任何增加都会给公众带来严重的困难，尤其是那些每年厨房消耗不少于10万吨煤炭的穷人。

一位经销商强调说：“因此，当1937年9月售价为每吨37美元的无烟煤，本月批发价跃升至每吨108美元时，其深远影响便显而易见。”

同样，烟煤的价格也 skyrocketing（原文不清，意指飙升）。从1937年初每吨18.50美元的批发报价，价格在9月份攀升至约每吨70美元，并自本月1日以来又上涨了20美元。

煤气、电费上调

煤炭成本上涨也以同样显著的方式影响了通常使用煤气和电力的较富裕家庭。回顾过去一个月，公用事业公司在消费者账单上征收了80%至120%不等的附加费。给出的涨价原因之一是煤炭价格稳步上涨。

关于将煤炭运往上海的运费，鸿基销售有限公司（Hongay Sales Ltd.）在战前从印度支那运输只需支付每吨2美元。目前，该公司每吨支付10先令，按昨日的汇率计算，约合国币27元。

总体而言，发现其他进口商，包括开滦矿务局和其他主要经销商，不得不支付比以前高得多的运费。鸿基销售有限公司可被视为典型代表。

（批：刘 10/13）

page_data.en:
Magnitude Shown
The magnitude of bituminous
coal consumption in Shanghai is
shown in the fact that the Shang-
hai Power Company, undoubtedly
the largest single user, burns about
50,000 tons each month in the pro-
duction of electricity. Of this
amount the company purchases one
half from the Kailan Mining
Administration while the other half
is either shipped here from the
United States or from Calcutta.
Other industries, including the
textile, chemical and shipping, also
are huge consumers. In all, they
require from upwards of 2,000,000
tons of bituminous coal a year.
As against these figures, Shang-
hailanders require approximately
500,000 tons of anthracite or hard
coal a year. Most of this amount
goes into private use although a
negligible quantity is supplied to
the small industrial establishments.
Bituminous coal comes principal-
ly from North China largely im-
ported to Shanghai by the Kailan
Mining Administration. Supplies
brought here by this company alone
totals no less than 1,000,000 tons
annually.
War Affects Supply
Other suppliers of soft coal in
Shanghai include the Ke? Loung
Company which imports Formosan
coal. This firm is responsible for
about one-fifth of the entire coal
supply in the city.
To date, Calcutta coal supplies
the balance of the city's need with
the exception of a small quantity
of coal from Shantung which
Japanese firms are importing to
the city. But in view of the pre-
sent war situation in Europe, deal-
ers are not at all certain that the
Calcutta supply will continue to
come regularly.
By far the largest anthracite coal
importer is the Hongay Sales Ltd.,
which alone sells more than three-
quarters of the requirement here
to the people. This firm obtains
its coal from the Hongay Mines in
Indo-China and brings it here on
chartered bottoms. Other com-
panies, all supplying the city with
Indo-China coal, include the Dong-
trieu Company which imports about
40,000 tons annually, Keleao Com-
pany, Uaokhe Company and the
Port Courbet Company.
page_data.zh:
规模显现

上海烟煤消费量的巨大规模体现在以下事实：上海电力公司无疑是最大的单一用户，每月在发电过程中燃烧约50,000吨。在此数量中，该公司一半从开滦矿务局购买，另一半则从美国或加尔各答运抵此处。

其他行业，包括纺织、化工和航运业，也是巨大的消费者。总的来说，它们每年需要200多万吨烟煤。

与此相比，上海居民每年大约需要50万吨无烟煤或硬煤。大部分用于私人用途，尽管有微不足道的数量供应给小型工业企业。

烟煤主要来自华北，主要由开滦矿务局进口到上海。仅该公司运抵此处的供应量每年就不少于100万吨。

战争影响供应

上海其他的软煤供应商包括进口台湾煤炭的 Ke? Loung Company（原文不清，音译：克隆公司？）。该公司负责全市煤炭供应总量的约五分之一。

迄今为止，除日本公司进口到本市的少量山东煤炭外，加尔各答的煤炭供应满足了本市剩余的需求。但鉴于欧洲目前的战争局势，经销商完全不确定加尔各答的供应能否继续定期到达。

迄今为止最大的无烟煤进口商是鸿基销售有限公司，仅该公司就向本市人民销售了超过四分之三的需求量。该公司从印度支那的鸿基煤矿（Hongay Mines）获取煤炭，并通过租船运抵此处。其他同样向本市供应印度支那煤炭的公司包括每年进口约40,000吨的 Dongtrieu Company（音译：东潮公司）、Keleao Company（音译：格劳公司）、Uaokhe Company（音译：乌奥克公司）以及 Port Courbet Company（音译：库尔贝港公司）。

NORTH CHINA COAL
COMPANY OPENS
Joint Sino-Japanese
Group Will Operate
Fuel Production
PEKING, Oct. 9.—With the idea
of exercising control over the pro-
duction and distribution of coal in
North China, a North China Coal
Control Company will be opened
before the end of this year with a
joint Sino-Japanese capital of
about $120,000,000.
The North China Development
Company, the liaison office of the
Asia Development Board and the
Provisional Government are now
discussing the technical details
relative to the inauguration of the

connecting Tatung in Shansi and
Tangku is expected to be started
within the year. The projected
railway is 500 kilometres in length
and is being built for expediting
coal shipments to Japan, which is
said to require 7,000,000 tons of
coal every year, it is added.—

公司开业

Shantung Coal

The first consignment of Hsing-chung coal, from South Shantung, will be shipped from Tsingtao to Japan soon, the Nikkan Kogyo announces.
The Hsingchung Coal Mines, situated near the Lincheng-Taier-chwang section of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway, have been provisionally repaired by the Japanese, after the mines had suffered some damage during the battle of Taierchwang.

Shanghai Power Co.,
Buys U.S. Navy Coal

Calcutta Supplies This
Port During Hostilities

London, Nov. 20.
Arrangements for a shipment of
40,000 tons of coal for the Shanghai
Power Company from San Francisco
in British vessels have been made, the
"Financial Times" learned.
Tonnage was booked in London.
The cargo of coal will be handled by
five vessels at a freight rate of U.S.$3

the coal from the United States Navy

Calcutta at present for coal supplies.

Shanghai thus far during 1938 totalled
150,000 tons compared with only 7,500
tons exported to Shanghai in 1937.
The shipment from San Francisco

据《金融时报》获悉，已安排通过英国船只从旧金山向上海电力公司运送4万吨煤炭。

Coal Supply
In Shanghai
Said Adequate

600,000 Tons Expected
To Be Used Monthly
During Winter

Although Shanghai does not have an abundant stock of coal, it will not face a shortage of the fuel in the coming five cold months, it was learned from reliable sources.

While many are showing renewed interest in the local coal situation, in view of the advent of cold weather, THE CHINA PRESS learned that an ample stock of coal is available in Shanghai and more is coming from abroad. In other words, the situation is not so acute as many may think.

The present stock of coal stored in Shanghai was placed at more than 100,000 tons by an official of a well-known mining company. For the month of November, at least 150,000 tons are expected to arrive here from North China, Australia, Africa, and India.

The above figures apply only to bituminous or soft coal, but the situation of anthracite or hard coal will not be tense either, since there are at least 50,000 tons in store now. About 80,000 tons more of hard coal are expected here for this month, it was said.

600,000 Tons Burned

THE CHINA PRESS was informed that for the five cold months—between November and March—Shanghai consumes about 600,000 tons of coal, and about this amount will be imported here. The coal comes from the following sources:

The Kailan Mining Administration, whose yearly output is 5 to 6 million tons, will supply Shanghai with 350,000 tons. Imported coal from abroad for the next five months will total to 150,000 tons. The Nee Tai Shing and Company, Ltd., believed to be the biggest Chinese coal dealer in Shanghai, has lately imported 80,000 tons, while other local dealers will have an aggregate stock of 250,000. This would make a sum total of 803,000 tons of coal available for the winter, which will cover the quantity to be consumed here.

No Coal Shortage

“No, I do not see any possibility or probability that Shanghai will face a shortage in coal for this winter,” the informant said. Questioned why so many Chinese householders complain of their inability to buy soft coal at a reasonable price, he continued:

“That is due to the fact that local Chinese coal dealers are spreading wild rumors of the impending shortage in coal. This resulted in a hike of coal prices on the local market.”

Apart from that, another reason why the prices of soft and hard coal made such a steep increase was because of the reduced output of coal mines located in North China, Shansi and Honan, it was stated. As a consequence, Shanghai is compelled to import the fuel from abroad. The depreciated Chinese currency and freight expenses are responsible for the increase, too.

2,000,000 Tons Consumed

It was learned that the best quality of hard coal is selling at $48 per ton, while soft coal is selling at $42, freight included.

Normally, Shanghai burns about 2,000,000 tons of coal, but this year, due to the increase in population and concentration of factories here, as much as 3,500,000 tons are needed, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

Of the latter figure, the Shanghai Power Company, which consumes the largest quantity of coal in Shanghai, requires about 500,000 tons.

The informant was of the opinion that it was possible to reopen the mines located in the Japanese-occupied areas in the interior, especially in Honan and Shansi. But this will take place some months later, he added.

《大美晚报》。
1938年11月6日

据称上海
煤炭供应
充足

冬季每月
预计消耗
60万吨

虽然上海的煤炭储备并不丰富，但从可靠消息来源获悉，在接下来的五个寒冷月份里，上海不会面临燃料短缺。

尽管随着寒冷天气的到来，许多人对本地煤炭状况重新表现出关注，但《大美晚报》获悉，上海有充足的煤炭库存，且更多煤炭正从国外运来。换句话说，情况并不像许多人想象的那样严峻。

一家知名矿业公司的一位官员表示，上海目前的煤炭库存超过10万吨。预计11月份至少有15万吨煤炭将从华北、澳大利亚、非洲和印度运抵此处。

上述数据仅适用于烟煤或软煤，但无烟煤或硬煤的情况也不会紧张，因为目前至少有5万吨库存。据说，本月还将有约8万吨硬煤运抵此处。

燃烧60万吨

《大美晚报》获悉，在11月至3月这五个寒冷月份期间，上海消耗约60万吨煤炭，届时也将进口大致相同数量的煤炭。煤炭来源如下：

开滦矿务局年产量为500万至600万吨，将向上海供应35万吨。未来五个月从国外进口的煤炭总量将达到15万吨。尼泰盛有限公司（Nee Tai Shing and Company, Ltd.）被认为是上海最大的中国煤商，最近进口了8万吨，而其他本地经销商的总库存为25万吨。这将使冬季可用的煤炭总量达到80.3万吨，足以覆盖此地的消耗量。

无煤炭短缺

“不，我看不到上海今年冬天面临煤炭短缺的任何可能性或概率，”消息人士说。当被问及为何如此多的中国家庭抱怨无法以合理价格买到软煤时，他继续说道：

“这是由于本地中国煤商散布即将出现煤炭短缺的谣言所致。这导致本地市场煤炭价格上涨。”

除此之外，软煤和硬煤价格大幅上涨的另一个原因是位于华北、山西和河南的煤矿产量减少。因此，上海被迫从国外进口燃料。中国货币贬值和运费也是导致价格上涨的原因。

消耗200万吨

据悉，最优质的硬煤售价为每吨48美元，而软煤售价为每吨42美元（含运费）。

《大美晚报》获悉，正常情况下，上海每年燃烧约200万吨煤炭，但今年由于人口增加和工厂在此集中，需要多达350万吨。

在后一个数字中，上海电力公司作为上海最大的煤炭消耗户，需要约50万吨。

消息人士认为，重新开放内地日军占领区的煤矿是可能的，特别是在河南和山西。但他补充说，这将在几个月后发生。

Ample Supply
Of Coal Said

Tons From India

《字林西报》，
1938年11月4日
据称本地
煤炭供应
充足
11月 shipments 也
很繁重；6万吨
来自印度
大量
硬煤运抵

随着上海迎来首次寒冷天气，人们对城市可用煤炭供应表示了极大关注。昨日获悉，这里有充足的煤炭供应以满足所有当前需求，且大量货物正在途中。

超过10万吨软煤已卸在上海并入库储存，预计11月份的运量将在15万吨左右。硬煤的情况 somewhat similar，据称目前有5万吨的储备供应。预计11月份硬煤运量将达到8万吨。

不包括电力公司
上述数字不包括上海电力公司卸货或订购的供应品，该公司消耗的燃料比上海任何其他工厂都多。

战事改变上海煤炭状况的方式体现在这样一个事实：仅11月份就有约6万吨软煤将从加尔各答运抵此处。在麻烦发生之前，上海主要依赖中国的煤田供应软煤，而不得不从更远的地方获取自然大大推高了价格。

进口成本
昨日在此采访的一位经销商估计，在上海卸下软煤的成本超过每吨40美元。据说按贬值的中国货币计算的实际购买价格为34.70美元，而关税和卸货费用另占6美元。据说，加尔各答煤炭目前在上海的零售价约为每吨42美元。

最优质的硬煤现在售价为每吨48美元，同品质的小块煤售价为45美元。此外，上海的煤球行业规模变得非常大，每月生产约2.6万吨此类燃料。
在战事爆发前，每月仅销售约1万吨，增长是由于人口增长以及对更好等级燃料索要更高价格所致。
（批注：R
Lile
C 4/11）

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 8 1938

Coal Prices Not Expected
To Show Marked Increase

Shanghai Believed Not Facing Coal Shortage
As Large Quantities Are Being Imported
From Australia And India

Although a large number of local households has begun, in view of the fast approach of cold weather to stock up coal for future household use. Shanghai will not face a shortage in coal, THE CHINA PRESS learned yesterday.

Nor will the coal prices in local markets register a marked increase as time passes on.

According to an officer of the Shanghai Municipal Council, several coal importers in Shanghai are importing large quantities of coal from Australia and particularly India for local consumption.

This newly-imported coal, if sold at $46 per ton as it probably will be, will yield a profit of not more than 10 per cent to the importers, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

Profiteering Denied

Current reports stating that many local coal merchants are making exorbitant increases in coal prices and thereby gain huge profits are refuted by the S.M.C. officer as well as an agent of a well-known mining administration.

Although it is true that the local price of household coal has increased to some $40 and $50 per ton as compared with last year's price of $20, the increase is only natural in view of the depreciation of Chinese currency and the foreign sources of the coal.

3,000,000 Tons

In normal times Shanghai consumes more than three million tons of coal, but now because of the suspension of operation of various factories caused by the war, the amount of coal consumed is only some two million tons.

Again, while formerly all the required amount of coal could be produced by Chinese and foreign mines located in China, this is found impossible due to the disruption of communications.

Of the 2,000,000 tons of coal to be consumed in Shanghai, well over half must be obtained from abroad, it is learned. Importing coal from abroad raises the prices due to freight. This, combined with the low Chinese exchange rates, naturally increases the prices of coal in Shanghai and anywhere else in China.

Reopening Of Coal Fields

It was suggested that the Shanghai Municipal Council, through consular channels, urge the reopening of certain coal fields in the interior in order that Shanghai may enjoy the normal supply. Several of these coal fields are located in Japanese-occupied areas.

This plan, according to the coal agent interviewed, would seem inadvisable for the time being, due to the present unsettled political and industrial conditions here.

DJ Henderson 4/2
C 5/10
8/10
